FL-005.label: Duplicate detection at creation, and outright removal of deprecated memories so they never collide with new ones.
FL-005.walk: `/remember` the same fact twice; the second is caught as a duplicate rather than stored again.
FL-005.observed: Real GPT-4.1 mini /remember exact re-save returned Already known - reinforced, advancing the existing amber-prism revision instead of adding another active memory.

FL-019.label: One-tap removal of an injected memory, with near-miss memories just below the cutoff shown so they can be added back.
FL-019.walk: At the gate, tap × on one memory and add one near-miss back; the count line updates.
FL-019.observed: Count line changed to 1 removed / 1 added after a near-miss veto and another near-miss add. Default removal of an injected real memory was also walked separately. This is partial: the exact combined injected-remove plus near-add sequence was not captured in one gate.

FL-020.label: A one-tap removal at the gate means 'not relevant' by default.
FL-020.walk: Tap × on a gate row; the removal is recorded as 'not relevant'.
FL-020.observed: Tapped the injected amber-prism row's default remove control. The resulting real memory history records inject/commit:removed:not_relevant at r6; no wrong/never modifier was selected.

FL-031.label: The gate as a visualization-plus-input module showing each memory's injection score.
FL-031.walk: The gate overlay shows each memory's injection score and takes removals.
FL-031.observed: Real gate displayed the injection total and component bars; default removal was accepted before Continue. The amber-prism revision records not_relevant feedback.

FL-033.label: Constitution: A near-miss 'never show this' veto (Aug 21 leak-fix packet).
FL-033.walk: Press and hold × on a near-miss; it never reappears in that thread's near-misses.
FL-033.observed: Accessible More options on the near-miss removal control opened Wrong/Never; Never removed the north-gate suggestion from subsequent trace and turn. The native pointer-hold gesture itself was not successfully demonstrated; handler tests are not substituted for that walk.

FL-038.label: A cheap 80/20 duplicate check at memory creation, keeping the agent's memory work under 10% of build run time.
FL-038.walk: Save a fact already in the Palace; the save comes back as a duplicate at once, without the agent reading other memories.
FL-038.observed: Real exact re-save returned Already known - reinforced through the save path, without an agent search/read of other memories. The same active memory advanced its revision.

FL-042.label: Constitution: 'Already known — reinforced' on re-saves; rejected candidates remembered and never re-proposed without material change (gate-day).
FL-042.walk: Re-save a known fact; the reply says 'already known — reinforced'; reject a candidate and re-save it unchanged; it is not proposed again.
FL-042.observed: Real known-fact re-save reinforced. In the isolated fixture, rejected the copper-compass seed in the UI, then re-offered the unchanged body in changed Markdown: queue stayed clear. Separate extraction receipts show cards=[] and duplicate_count=1 after rejection.

FL-045.label: Same-memory detection by encoding and retrieving, not exact wording.
FL-045.walk: Save a rephrased known fact; it is recognized as the same memory instead of duplicating.
FL-045.observed: Rephrased the real drawer-eight fact and received Already known - reinforced on the same amber-prism memory (r4), with no duplicate active head.

FL-048.label: A permanent back-test table of every human add and removal of a memory, as the training data for the injection algorithm.
FL-048.walk: Remove a memory at the gate; a new row for it appears in the back-test table.
FL-048.observed: Real gate feedback created its removal revision, and the fixture has recorded learner history. A new matching row in the visible back-test table was not demonstrated; verification-principal feedback is correctly excluded from authentic training.

FL-197.label: Spend and Palace state reads use the calling principal; only the configured owner can request the whole Palace.
FL-197.walk: In a verification daemon, open Spend and Palace State and see only that principal's receipts and counts. In a local fixture, compare the configured owner's whole-Palace view. Request scope=palace as the verification principal and see a plain 403. Keep owner-rack captures out of evidence.
FL-197.observed: Real verification UI displayed only its own spend/counts and owner-only learning notice, with global database size unavailable. Three explicit scope=palace requests returned plain 403s. The isolated fixture owner comparison is in fixture-owner-scopes.json; no owner rack was captured.

FL-169.label: Client and cloud versions stay sync-locked or backward compatible, following industry practice, so version differences feel seamless.
FL-169.walk: Start a client whose version differs from the cloud Palace's; it either keeps working or refuses with a plain version message.
FL-169.observed: A clean 0.1.13 client performed a typed principal-scoped spend read against the released 0.1.14 Palace and returned its two disposable threads. version-compatibility.json records the mismatch and success.

FL-195.label: The feature ledger generates coverage reports and requires evidence for the rows affected by a build.
FL-195.walk: Compute the composer fix's impact with --paths and see attunement rows; push a branch touching socket.ts and observe the hook print rows and write impacted.json; observe a DONE handoff without screenshots fail CI, then verify complete evidence passes.
FL-195.observed: Ran 22 ledger tests including real-Git impact/pre-push/standalone evidence and negative missing-screenshot cases, plus 8 rule tests. --paths harness/web/src/socket.ts mapped FL-104/117/120, and actual release-branch pushes printed the impact bell and wrote impacted.json. Complete evidence is checked at this handoff.

FL-196.label: The rules machine checks citations, frozen law, product vocabulary, seed states and packet precedents.
FL-196.walk: Remove a guard citation on a disposable branch and observe CI fail; change a frozen axiom and observe the freeze step fail; restore both and observe Rules pass. The master ADR check remains red until the owner applies the citation patch.
FL-196.observed: Eight rule tests exercised citation removal and frozen-law mutation in disposable copies and restored green checks; 22 ledger tests also passed. Current freeze/ADR/seeds/precedents checks pass. The historical pending owner citation is already resolved upstream.

FL-002.label: Memory units have a length cap; a memory over the cap is shortened to fit as one memory, and it is split only when it holds more than one distinct fact, with the split logged.
FL-002.walk: /remember a 300-token paragraph holding one fact; one memory lands, shortened to the cap; a paragraph holding two facts lands as two.
FL-002.observed: Sent a 286-token single-fact paragraph (approximately 300): one shortened jade-key memory of 13 tokens landed. A two-fact paragraph produced distinct instrument-museum and glassworks memories. real-memory-snapshot.json records the resulting bodies/token counts.

FL-003.label: Constitution: Every edit is a compare-and-swap revision, deletions are tombstones, and a write conflict is a first-class event (founding ADRs).
FL-003.walk: Edit a memory body; the memory shows a new revision and the old revision is still retrievable.
FL-003.observed: Edited the real amber-prism body from drawer seven to drawer eight. Expanded history shows r1/r2 old bodies and r3 edited body; the old revisions remain retrievable after later reinforcement/removal feedback.

FL-015.label: Constitution: Typed edges between memories (merged from, supersedes, contradicts, and richer kinds at creation and curation) with a depth-limited traversal for the graph and the scorer (SD-057).
FL-015.walk: Open the Memory Graph on a curated memory; typed edges (merged from, supersedes, contradicts) are drawn to its relatives.
FL-015.observed: Earlier same-packet real curator/fixture walk displayed merged_from and supersedes relationships. A contradicts edge was not demonstrated. Retained phase-one evidence is explicitly partial and is not relabeled as a fresh full walk.

FL-021.label: The memory visualizer shows the hyperparameters and lets the user go in and tweak memories.
FL-021.walk: Open the memory visualizer; the hyperparameters are displayed and a memory can be edited from there.
FL-021.observed: Earlier same-packet real graph editor changed the amber-prism body and showed scoring parameters. This resumed walk also edited Telescope guide from Lena to Nora (r3) in the fixture graph; final parameters include minimum match .55 and share .10. Original feature-named capture plus graph-edit-parameters.jpg are retained.

FL-026.label: The keyword, project key and origin path columns on a memory are filled in and factored into scoring.
FL-026.walk: Open a memory card; keyword, project and origin path are filled, and the score breakdown shows them counting.
FL-026.observed: Real memory card has keywords, project and origin WHERE. The fixture gate's expanded breakdown shows Keyword, Project and Where contributions, alongside other raw/weighted components.

FL-162.walk: On a fresh machine, follow the splash repo's install steps; you are asked for a GCP credential and an OpenRouter key and nothing else before the app comes up.
